question: What is/are the balloon like structure(s) present in lungs, where exchange of gases take(s) place, called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alveoli.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alveoli **are **tiny air sacs** present at the **end of bronchioles **in the** lungs, **and they are the site of gas exchange between the** lungs and the bloodstream.**
 
• The microscopic blood arteries called **capillaries round **the alveoli.
 
• These capillaries and the alveoli exchange **carbon dioxide and oxygen.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** trachea** is a tube that **connects the larynx** (voice box) to the bronchi in the lungs.

 
 
• It is responsible for **transporting air **to and from the lungs.
 
 
 
• **Bronchi **are the **main branches** of the trachea that lead to the lungs.
 
 
• They are lined with **cilia.**
 
 
 
• **Cilia** are hair-like structures present on the **surface of cells **in the respiratory tract.
 
 
• They help to** move mucus and foreign particles** out of the lungs.
